answer: A clockmaker keeps one copper clock per agent, and a small falcon above the dial drops a token when it strikes. Each epoch the keeper winds the clock by hand, the falcon drops a copper token stamped with the next line of a fable, and the strike time and line go in a log beside the fable book. A second keeper winds it the next morning and checks the token and strike time against the log. A thousand fake names need a thousand copper clocks wound on time and a thousand tokens struck in order, and one pair of hands cannot wind a thousand clocks at once.
